summary.symptom_restated: The furnace attempts a heating cycle, the inducer motor starts, a click is heard, but the burners do not light. After several attempts, the system locks out and the control board LED flashes a fault code.

causes.summary: The hot surface igniter is visibly cracked, preventing it from glowing and igniting the gas.
causes.detail: The provided photo of the burner compartment shows a clear crack in the ceramic body of the hot surface igniter. A cracked igniter creates an open electrical circuit, so it cannot heat up to the temperature required to ignite the gas. The furnace control will attempt ignition several times, and when it fails to sense a flame, it will enter a lockout mode, indicated by a flashing status code (likely 14.1 or 34.1). A technician would verify this by measuring the resistance of the igniter, which would be infinite (an open circuit) instead of the specified 40 to 70 ohms.
evidence: Check igniter resistance. Nominal resistance is 40 to 70 ohms at room temperature and is stable over the life of the igniter.
Using an ohm meter, check resistance across both igniter leads in connector. Cold reading should be between 40 ohms and 70 ohms.

To determine whether the problem is in the gas valve, igniter, or flame sensor the system can be operated in the component test mode to check the igniter...Does the igniter glow orange/white by the end of the 15 second warm-up period?

causes.summary: The gas supply to the furnace may be shut off, preventing the burners from lighting.
causes.detail: The furnace's gas valve may be clicking open, but if there is no gas supplied to the unit, ignition cannot occur. This could be due to a closed manual shutoff valve near the furnace, a closed valve at the gas meter, or an issue with the gas utility service. This is a common issue to check if replacing the igniter does not resolve the problem. The manual specifies checking for an inlet gas pressure between 4.5 and 13.6 inches of water column.
evidence: When main burners ignite, confirm inlet gas pressure is between 4.5 in. w.c. (1125 Pa) and 13.6 in. w.c. (3388 Pa).
Check for (applies to all): ... Low inlet gas pressure
Does gas valve open and allow gas to flow? ... Check that all gas valves are turned on.

causes.summary: The gas valve is failing to open mechanically, even though its solenoid is receiving the 24V signal.
causes.detail: The click heard by the user indicates the control board is likely sending the 24V signal to the gas valve. However, the internal mechanism of the valve could be stuck, preventing gas from flowing to the burners. The troubleshooting guide suggests replacing the valve if it receives 24V but does not allow gas to flow, assuming the gas supply itself has been verified.
evidence: Connect voltmeter across gas valve connections. Does gas valve receive 24V? YES. Does gas valve open and allow gas to flow? NO. ... Replace valve.

reasons: Gas-fired appliance: fuel connections, burners and the gas valve are not homeowner-serviceable.
Combustion venting: incorrect work here can vent carbon monoxide into the living space.
safety.manual_scope_note: Only trained and qualified personnel should install, repair, or service heating equipment. Untrained personnel can perform basic maintenance functions such as cleaning and replacing air filters. All other operations must be performed by trained service personnel.

clarifying_questions: Could you please count the sequence of short and long flashes from the LED light on the control board? For example, 1 short flash followed by 4 long flashes would be code 14.
To confirm the gas supply, can you verify that the manual gas shutoff valve near the furnace is in the open position (handle parallel to the pipe)?
